bullets.title: Princess Mononoke
bullets.note:
(Amazon: [English](https://www.amazon.com/Princess-Mononoke-English-Language-Crudup/dp/B081F8K9ZX/ref=tmm_aiv_swatch_0?_encoding=UTF8&qid=1617306661&sr=8-1), [Japanese](https://www.amazon.com/Princess-Mononoke-Japanese-Language-Matsuda/dp/B081RC3212/ref=sr_1_3?dchild=1&keywords=princess+mononoke+japanese&qid=1617157045&sr=8-3); [iTunes](https://itunes.apple.com/us/movie/princess-mononoke/id1485476692?cmp=rt_where_to_watch)). This animated film, from the legendary [Hayao Miyazaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayao_Miyazaki) and his [Studio Ghibli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Ghibli), has thousands of five-star reviews on Amazon and elsewhere. I was in Tokyo for its opening weekend in 1997, and I recall being astonished by the neverending lines of theatergoers bending around city blocks, eagerly awaiting the first showings. It dramatically outearned _The Lost World: Jurassic Park_ at the box office, which opened the same weekend. Even if you don’t watch the entire film, [the original Japanese trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rPs1C4277wE) is worth watching. Of course, I prefer the Japanese version with English subtitles, but the English dubbed version has excellent voice actors. If you enjoy _Princess Mononoke_, you might as well pair it with [_Spirited Away_](https://www.amazon.com/Spirited-English-Language-Daveigh-Chase/dp/B081GFFJLN/)—likely my favorite movie of all time—and for more on the process of storytelling genius Hayao Miyazaki, I highly recommend his accompanying [_The Art of Spirited Away_](https://www.amazon.com/Art-Spirited-Away-Hayao-Miyazaki/dp/1569317771) book_.

bullets.title: UCSF establishes the Neuroscape Psychedelics Division with $6.4M in funding
bullets.note: This is huge news for the burgeoning field of psychedelic medicine. Dr. Robin Carhart-Harris ([@RCarhartHarris](https://twitter.com/RCarhartHarris)), a renowned psychedelic researcher best known for his work at the [Centre for Psychedelic Research at Imperial College London](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/psychedelic-research-centre/), is joining Neuroscape as the director of the Psychedelics Division, and he’ll be working alongside the founder of [Neuroscape](https://neuroscape.ucsf.edu/psychedelics), Dr. Adam Gazzaley ([@adamgazz](https://twitter.com/adamgazz)). Prior Neuroscape (previously known as Gazzaley Lab) research has been featured on the cover of _Nature_ ([cover image and synopsis](https://www.al.com/breaking/2013/09/game_changer_research_shows_vi.html), [research description](https://www.nature.com/news/gaming-improves-multitasking-skills-1.13674)), and this dream team is perfectly poised to address fundamental questions about psychedelic therapies largely untouched by research to date. To learn more, please hear [my brand-new podcast with Adam](https://tim.blog/2021/03/30/adam-gazzaley-2/?utm-source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf), which was released this week. If you’d like to support their ambitious plans, as I am, you can donate cash or securities by visiting [this page](https://neuroscape.ucsf.edu/get-involved/donate/), and you can donate cryptocurrencies by emailing [neuroscape@ucsf.edu](mailto:neuroscape@ucsf.edu).

bullets.title: Lost in Thought
bullets.creator: David Kortava for Harper’s Magazine_
bullets.note: for _Harper’s Magazine_. I would have dismissed this article were it not for my personal experience with retraumatization and breakdown at a silent retreat in 2017. I recount this experience at roughly [12:11](https://overcast.fm/+Kebu8teN4/12:10) of [my podcast episode on healing from childhood abuse](https://tim.blog/2020/09/14/how-to-heal-trauma/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf). This is a very well-researched piece on the largely ignored risks of meditation and, more specifically, the enhanced risks of longer retreats for some populations. I still regularly meditate, but I do find there to be a point of diminishing returns, as well as a point (i.e., extended retreats) where the risk-benefit ratio can change dramatically.
